tagline: A 4-million-person metro built around a giant inland lake, with a daily catamaran commute already running — and the most famous sunset in southern Brazil waiting to become a signature water route.
summary: Porto Alegre sits where the Jacuí delta opens into Lago Guaíba, a broad, sheltered inland lake that separates the capital from the fast-growing cities of Guaíba and Eldorado do Sul on the far shore. Uniquely for Brazil, the water-commuting habit is already adopted: CatSul's catamarans have crossed Porto Alegre–Guaíba daily since 2011, beating the congested BR-116 road loop, while tour boats work the Jacuí delta islands and the lake's celebrated sunset. After the historic May 2024 floods severed roads for weeks, the state began investing in waterway 'resilience routes' — making clean, fast, shallow-draft marine mobility a public-infrastructure conversation, not just a leisure one.

demand_signals.label: Adopted water-commuting habit
demand_signals.value: CatSul carries ~1,700 passengers/day between Porto Alegre and Guaíba on three catamarans (170 + 120 + 120 seats), a 30-minute crossing
demand_signals.note: Daily intermunicipal service operating since 2011 — this is a modernise-an-adopted-habit market, not a create-demand market

demand_signals.label: Fast early adoption
demand_signals.value: 370,000 passengers in the first six months of catamaran operation (2012)
demand_signals.note: The crossing found its ridership immediately once a fast water option existed

demand_signals.label: Resilient base demand
demand_signals.value: 314,000 passengers in 2020 despite the pandemic cutting trips 44%
demand_signals.note: Even in the worst year on record the corridor kept six-figure ridership

demand_signals.label: Network expansion pipeline
demand_signals.value: Metroplan is studying new catamaran routes; Eldorado do Sul, Esteio, Cachoeirinha and Gravataí have formally signalled interest, and Eldorado do Sul began a R$5.2M dredging project (Dec 2025) to open a waterway link to Porto Alegre
demand_signals.note: The state's post-flood 'Rotas de Resiliência' plan (Dec 2025) includes an Eldorado do Sul–Porto Alegre waterway route — public money is moving toward more water transit
demand_signals.source: Prefeitura de Eldorado do Sul; O Sul; Governo do RS Rotas de Resiliência (Dec 2025)

demand_signals.label: Sunset and delta tourism market
demand_signals.value: The Cisne Branco tour boat runs year-round from the Cais do Porto — R$50 delta-island cruises up to R$195 premium sailings, including dedicated sunset happy-hour departures
demand_signals.note: The Guaíba sunset is Porto Alegre's signature postcard; an on-water sunset market already pays premium prices for slow diesel boats

demand_signals.label: Metro scale on the waterfront
demand_signals.value: Porto Alegre anchors a ~4.1M-person metropolitan region, and a 2014 field test found the catamaran the fastest link between the city centre and the Zona Sul
demand_signals.note: The revitalised waterfront (Orla do Guaíba, Cais Embarcadero, Parque do Pontal) has rebuilt the city's relationship with the lake

use_cases.title: Modernise the Guaíba crossing
use_cases.body: Replace and extend the diesel catamaran habit with quiet, zero-emission foiling shuttles on the proven Centro↔Guaíba and Pontal↔Guaíba lines — same 30-minute promise, smoother ride, no diesel plume over the lake, and fare economics no longer hostage to diesel prices (fuel was ~50% of the incumbent's operating cost in 2022).

use_cases.title: Flood-resilience waterway network
use_cases.body: The May 2024 floods cut road access to Eldorado do Sul and paralysed the metro area. The state's Rotas de Resiliência programme and Eldorado's dredging works are explicitly building waterway alternatives — shallow-draft (1.5 ft) electric shuttles are a natural fit for the delta's dredged channels and new resilience piers.

use_cases.title: Sunset flights and delta safaris
use_cases.body: Foiling sunset runs off the Gasômetro and silent, zero-wake cruises through the Delta do Jacuí state park islands (Ilha da Pintada's fishing village and waterfront restaurants) — upgrading a tour market that already sells out slow diesel sunset cruises.

use_cases.title: Event and innovation-district shuttles
use_cases.body: CatSul already lays on special Cais Embarcadero stops for South Summit Brazil each March. A premium foiling shuttle linking the Centro terminal, Cais Embarcadero and Píer Pontal turns the revitalised waterfront into a connected event campus.

journeys.from: Terminal Hidroviário de Porto Alegre (Cais Mauá, Armazém B3)
journeys.to: Terminal Hidroviário de Guaíba (Av. João Pessoa)
journeys.today: A 30-minute diesel catamaran (R$16.90) or a much longer drive around the BR-116/bridge loop in commuter traffic.
journeys.with_navier: The same trusted crossing, flying silently above the lake chop — no diesel, no wake, smoother than the road will ever be.

journeys.to: Guaíba sunset run (western shore and back)
journeys.today: A slow diesel happy-hour cruise (R$80–100) packed on weekends; most people watch the famous sunset from the crowded seawall.
journeys.with_navier: A silent foiling sunset flight across the lake's golden hour — the city's postcard moment, from the best seat on the water.

journeys.today: A one-hour loop on the Cisne Branco tour boat or a private lancha to the delta's fishing-village restaurants.
journeys.with_navier: A ten-minute zero-wake hop into the Delta do Jacuí state park — quiet enough for the protected wetlands, fast enough to make the islands a lunch destination.

journeys.today: A drive or bus up the riverside avenues; the 2014 GaúchaZH test already found the boat faster than the road to the Zona Sul.
journeys.with_navier: An eight-minute foiling commute along the revitalised Orla, stitching the Pontal district, the shopping piers and downtown into one waterfront.

journeys.today: BR-290 by road — the corridor that flooded in May 2024, cutting the city off for weeks; dredging for a waterway alternative began in Dec 2025.
journeys.with_navier: A shallow-draft electric shuttle on the state's planned resilience route, running whether or not the highway is dry.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire Lago Guaíba mesh is short-hop and sheltered — Centro↔Guaíba (~8 nm sailed), Gasômetro↔sunset runs (~6 nm), delta island spurs (~2 nm), Zona Sul marina hops (1–4 nm) — all trivially inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with marina and terminal charging available on both shores. Zero-wake foiling matters in the Delta do Jacuí protected wetlands.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Not required for the core lake network. If the network later extends down the Lagoa dos Patos toward Pelotas/Rio Grande (~140+ nm south, the state's historic steamer corridor), Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range covers it without any charging infrastructure en route.

competitive_landscape: CatSul (Grupo Ouro e Prata) is the incumbent and the proof of demand: three diesel catamarans (170/120/120 seats) on the Porto Alegre–Guaíba concession since 2011, ~1,700 passengers/day pre-flood, with student free-fare integration (Passe Fácil) and TEU metropolitan ticketing already accepted on the water. The Cisne Branco runs the tour market from the Cais do Porto. Pain points are real and documented: diesel is ~50% of the incumbent's cost base and drove repeated fare fights, the fleet is conventional (wake, noise, fuel smell), and service stops entirely when floods or post-flood debris hit — 67 days suspended in 2024. Demand evidence is strong; the experience and resilience layers are where the upgrade lives.
seasonality: Subtropical and year-round operable. Summers (Dec–Mar) are hot with long golden evenings — peak sunset and delta-tour season. Winters (Jun–Aug) are cool (~10°C) with morning fog on the lake but calm water. The lake kicks up short chop under southerly winds ('vento sul'), which foiling flies above. The honest operational note: Lago Guaíba is flood-prone — the record May 2024 flood (Guaíba gauge above 5.3 m) suspended all navigation for ~two months, and post-flood debris (trees, trunks) is a hazard every operator must manage with inspection and routing; the state's dredging and resilience-route investments are a direct response.
regulatory_note: Inland navigation is governed by the Brazilian Navy (Capitania Fluvial de Porto Alegre — vessel class, crew, survey). Metropolitan passenger transport, including the catamaran concession, is regulated by Metroplan (the state metropolitan planning foundation), with tariffs reviewed by AGERGS, the state public-services regulator — fares were adjusted +14.21% (Feb 2025) and +7.32% (Jun 2026) largely on diesel and payroll costs, an opening for electric operating economics. Portos RS is the port authority for the Cais Mauá waterfront. Metroplan has an active waterway plan (Plano Hidroviário do RS) and has publicly studied new catamaran routes, including a Beira-Rio stadium terminal.
signature_routes: Centro (Cais Mauá) ↔ Guaíba — the proven daily crossing, upgraded (signature)
Gasômetro / Cais Embarcadero ↔ Guaíba sunset run — southern Brazil's most famous sunset, from the water (signature)
Cais do Porto ↔ Ilha da Pintada / Delta do Jacuí islands — zero-wake delta safari (signature)
Centro ↔ Píer Pontal ↔ BarraShoppingSul — the Orla commuter string
Porto Alegre ↔ Eldorado do Sul — the state's flood-resilience waterway route

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of scheduled water mobility at national scale — the playbook for turning an existing ferry habit into a clean network.

precedents.where: Rio Grande do Sul (Rotas de Resiliência, Dec 2025)
precedents.why_it_matters: Post-flood public investment is actively building piers, dredged channels and waterway routes on Lago Guaíba — infrastructure a clean foiling fleet can ride on day one.
